text: Ten days after the production deploy, nothing about Driftwood's storefront app is broken. No alerts, no pages. But a routine Monday check of Azure Cost Analysis tells a different story.

This app was sized to run at about seventeen hundred fifty dollars a month. The forecast line is now pacing toward roughly twenty-four hundred sixty dollars, about forty percent over plan, with Azure Kubernetes Service as the dominant, growing line item.

Anomaly detection is already enabled on this subscription, but it learns what's normal from a workload's own spend history, and this app is only about ten days old. There isn't enough history yet for a baseline, which is why nothing paged Theo automatically.
No incident, no rollback, just a real question worth answering calmly: why is this app costing forty percent more than it was sized for? Next lesson traces that number back to its actual source.
